Urban Design & Planning

Rancho Palos Verdes Mixed-Use Overlay District

Location
Rancho Palos Verdes, CA
Firm
Dudek
Role
Consultant team: site feasibility studies, ADU comparison research, community outreach and workshops

Under the pressure of the State’s mandated Regional Housing Needs Allocation (RHNA), Rancho Palos Verdes was faced with the task of identifying potential methods of maximizing land use. As part of the consultant team, I conducted thorough site feasibility studies, researched how other cities allow for ADUs, and presented my findings to the city and the community through outreach and workshops. My findings were part of the final adopted Housing Element Update.

  • Site feasibility studies
  • ADU & JADU research
  • RHNA
  • Community outreach
  • Adopted Housing Element Update

01Site feasibility: Westmont Plaza

One site, tested against the City’s RM-22 zone and modified commercial (CG) standards, to see what the proposed Mixed-Use Overlay could really deliver.

5.9acres
300′×858′parcel
CGcurrent zone
  • Located at Western Avenue and Westmont Drive, outside the Western Avenue Specific Plan.
  • Currently retail, anchored by Smart and Final, and abutting Eastview Park.
  • Tested with the City’s RM-22 zone and modified CG development standards.
  • APN 7444-001-003.

Existing build and maximum envelope

02Two typologies tested

Test fits that show what each set of standards would actually build, with real projects as reference.

Option 1Activated commercial corner with townhomes

Townhomes with in-unit parking and condos at the corner, up to 36′.

Option 2Mixed-use podium and wrap

A podium building and a wrap building with structured parking, up to 36′.

03Development standards: current and studied

What changed between the existing CG zone and the standards used in the study.

StandardCurrent (CG zone)Studied
Lot coverageMaximum 50%Not required
Setbacks20′ abutting street, 10′ abutting non-residential, 20′ abutting residential with no parking allowedCommercial: 5′ front, 5′ side, 20′ rear with parking allowed. Residential: 25′ front, 25′ street side, 20′ rear
HeightAbove 16′ only by CUP; a height variation permit can allow up to 26′36′ before discretionary review; above 36′ by CUP
Open spacePrivate decks and balconies may count for up to 30% of the requirement35% of lot size, with the same 30% allowance for private decks and balconies
Building separation30′ where walls have openings, 10′ where they do not25′ where walls have openings, 10′ unchanged
Parking1 space per 200 SFMixed use: 1.5 spaces per home and 1 per 200 SF commercial, plus 25% guest parking

04Key takeaways

What the test fits told the City about its own standards.

  1. RM-22 is too restrictiveIt is the most accommodating multifamily standard the City has, and it still falls short.
  2. 36′ makes podium and wrap types infeasibleThose types are typically built to 60–70′.
  3. The View Preservation Ordinance is stricter stillIt limits height to 16′ along Western and 20′ along the park edge.
  4. Open space limits feasible densityRM-22’s 35% is the lightest of any RM zone, yet it is hard to meet at feasible densities.
  5. Parking standards need revisitingWith view and RM height limits in place, relaxing parking is one way to reduce barriers.
  6. Existing standards miss Housing Element densitiesCG and RM-22 together do not reach 25 homes per acre on this site.
  7. The CUP above 16′ is a strong deterrentIt discourages new development outright.
  8. MUX standards must depart from existing zonesHeight, parking, open space and lot coverage will all need to deviate.

05ADU & JADU research

Prepared for the City Council presentation of May 18, 2023 (draft): what state law requires, how Rancho Palos Verdes compares, and how neighboring cities handle ADUs.

Six years of state legislation

2016
  • SB 1069Streamlines approvals and limits parking and utility connection fees.
  • AB 2299Defines attached and detached ADUs and requires compliant local ordinances.
2017–18
  • SB 229Bars fees and requirements that discourage ADU development.
2019
  • AB 68One ADU plus one JADU per lot, with lighter parking and setback rules.
  • AB 881No owner-occupancy requirement and fewer excessive fees.
  • SB 13Limits fees, eases parking and allows attached and detached units.
2020–21
  • AB 3182Applications are deemed approved if the city has not acted within 60 days.
  • SB 58Compliant ADUs and JADUs must be approved within 60 days.
2022
  • AB 2221Front setbacks cannot block an 800 SF ADU; all permitting agencies must explain denials.
  • SB 89716′ minimum height limit, objective standards and no penalty for old unpermitted work.

HCD minimums at a glance

60 daysmaximum review time, then deemed approved
4′maximum side and rear setback
16′minimum height a city must allow
800 SFfloor a city must allow for an ADU
750 SFADUs below this pay no impact fees
500 SFmaximum size of a JADU

Before SB 9One single-family lot

Four ways to qualify, from the Los Angeles County ordinance

06Rancho Palos Verdes against the state standard

The City’s ordinance follows HCD closely. Where it differs is design, size and the View Ordinance.

TopicHCD standardRancho Palos Verdes
Unit sizeWithout an ordinance: 850 SF minimum, 1,000 SF for one bedroom, and cities should still allow 800 SF. With one: detached up to 1,200 SF, attached up to 50% of the primary home.Detached up to 50% of the primary home’s main floor area. 850 SF for one bedroom, 1,000 SF for more.
HeightNo limit in state law; cities may not go below 16′.Shall not exceed 16′.
DesignLeft to the local agency.Match the primary home. Entrance faces away from the nearest neighbor, windows at or above six feet on facades facing neighbors, and no roof decks.
Setbacks, parking, feesUp to 4′ side and rear, none for conversions. One space per unit or bedroom, with exemptions. No impact fees under 750 SF.Same as HCD.
AffordabilityEncouraged.Incentive programs under consideration in place of 10-year affordability covenants.

Special considerations for Rancho Palos Verdes

An “affected city”The Housing Crisis Act of 2019 applies, so local rules cannot reduce residential capacity.
Coastal zoneLocal Coastal Programs still apply to ADU permits until they are amended.
View OrdinanceThe Height Variation Permit and View Ordinance do not allow a 16′ ADU on every site.

07How comparable cities handle ADUs

Nine neighboring jurisdictions compared with the HCD standard.

CityUnit sizeSetbacksNotable
LomitaSimilar to HCD, but does not list every maximum.Same as HCDSeparate entrance not facing the alley; septic tanks not allowed.
Rolling Hills EstatesMax 850 SF, or 1,000 SF for one bedroom; 16′ height.Same as HCDAppears to read HCD minimums as maximums.
Long BeachMax 50% of the primary home, at least 800 SF; limited ADUs from 180 SF.5′ rear and sideSeparates Limited from Conforming ADUs; Conforming allows 25′ and two stories.
Hermosa BeachMax 850 SF, or 1,000 SF for one bedroom.4′ rear and side, 25′ frontWindows near property lines must be clerestory or obscure glass.
TorranceSame as HCDSame as HCDAllows ADUs only within one mile of high-quality transit corridors.
Redondo BeachSame as HCDSame as HCD; front setback of at least 10′ encouragedSeparate entrance required; separate driveway if the ADU abuts an alley.
CarsonDetached 1,200 SF; attached 850 SF, or 1,000 SF for one bedroom; JADU 500 SF.Same as HCDSpells out maximums by unit type.
Los AngelesAttached up to 50% of the home; detached 1,200 SF; JADU 500 SF.Same as HCDDetached allows two stories plus the zoning height.
Los Angeles CountyDetached 1,200 SF; JADU 500 SF; 25′ height or per plan.Under 4′ allowed with fire review; no windows within 3′ of the lineClearest charts and diagrams of any jurisdiction reviewed.

08Lessons learned

What the comparison suggested for Rancho Palos Verdes policy.

  1. Minimums read as maximumsSome cities treat the square footages and heights in state law as caps. These sections need updating to match the 2023 bills.
  2. Comparable cities follow HCD closelyFew of them go beyond the state guidelines.
  3. The View Ordinance can block the minimumsIt may prevent an ADU from reaching 800 SF, a 4′ setback and 16′ of height.
  4. Show the whole processA guide to applying for an ADU in Rancho Palos Verdes, including how denials work, would help applicants.
  5. Standards may be too restrictive for designCurrent development standards could limit how well an ADU can be designed.
